title: Indicator: Autoenvelope (channel)
description: Moving-average envelope (upper/lower bands) around EMA(13), used for profit-target zones and the exit rule 'price reaches upper band with Impulse Red'.

checklist.step: Decide the envelope-width calculation (avg % deviation from EMA) per docs/Analyse.md §4 — not yet pinned to an exact formula, confirm/decide before coding
Implement app/indicators/autoenvelope.py: pure function returning a DataFrame with 'mid', 'upper', 'lower' columns
Run pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing and confirm no regression

decisions.decision: Autoenvelope width = a trailing rolling average, over a `deviation_lookback` window (default 100 trading days), of each bar's absolute percentage deviation from EMA(13): `avg_pct_t = mean(|close_i - mid_i| / mid_i for i in [t - lookback + 1, t])`, where `mid = EMA(close, ema_period)`. Bands are a symmetric multiplicative envelope: `upper = mid * (1 + avg_pct)`, `lower = mid * (1 - avg_pct)`. Both `ema_period` (default 13) and `deviation_lookback` are function parameters, not hardcoded, so `portfolio-exit-rules` or future tuning can override them. `mid`/`upper`/`lower` are all returned with the same index as `close`; `upper`/`lower` are NaN for the first `deviation_lookback - 1` bars where the rolling window isn't yet full (a deliberate no-lookahead choice — see rejected alternatives below).
decisions.rationale: docs/Analyse.md §4 pins the shape ('EMA 13 ± avg % deviation') and its role (profit-target zone / overextension, feeding the exit rule 'price reaches upper band with Impulse Red' in §7) but not the exact window or whether the average is trailing, static, or asymmetric. Chose a trailing rolling average over a static (only-computed-once, e.g. over the whole history or a fixed calibration period) average because a static % would either bake in look-ahead bias (computed once using the full series, including future bars relative to any given point) or need to be pre-computed offline and hardcoded per ticker — neither fits the pure-function/no-I-O/no-global-state constraint this app's indicators are held to (docs/architecture/Backend.md §4), and an adaptive trailing window matches how Elder describes recalibrating channel width to recent price behavior in the book. Chose a symmetric band (single avg % applied to both sides) over separate upside/downside deviation stats (which Elder's manual channel-drawing technique in the book actually allows to differ) because Analyse.md's own phrasing is explicitly symmetric ('± avg % deviation', one term, not two) — an asymmetric variant would be inventing a parameter Analyse.md doesn't call for. Chose close-to-EMA percentage deviation (not high/low-to-EMA) for consistency with how every other daily indicator in this app (Force Index, MACD-Histogram) is keyed off closing price, and because Analyse.md's table doesn't mention high/low for this row. Picked 100 trading days (~5 months) as the default lookback: long enough to smooth out single-event volatility spikes and reflect 'several months of representative price action' (the interval Elder's book describes eyeballing when manually sizing a channel), short enough to still adapt across a market regime change within roughly two quarters, and it comfortably fits within the ~200-trading-day minimum history requirement already set by Analyse.md §8. Rejected shorter windows tied to existing indicator periods (e.g. 13 or 26, matching the EMA periods, or 20 to mirror a Bollinger-style default) as arbitrary reuse with no basis in Analyse.md and prone to being whipsawed by short-term volatility bursts, which would make the profit-target zone too noisy to be useful for the exit rule it feeds. NaN before the window is full (rather than an expanding-window average for the warm-up period) was chosen to keep the deviation estimate honest — an expanding average over e.g. only 2-3 bars would be a statistically meaningless 'average' and could produce a misleadingly tight or wide band right when a ticker's history is thinnest; downstream consumers (portfolio-exit-rules) already need to handle NaN indicator values during any warm-up period (EMA26, MACD signal line, etc.), so this doesn't introduce a new failure mode. Rejected alternatives, summarized: static/whole-series average % deviation (look-ahead bias); asymmetric upside/downside bands (not what Analyse.md's '±' phrasing specifies); high/low-based deviation instead of close-based (inconsistent with every other close-keyed daily indicator in this app); shorter lookbacks (13/20/26 days) reused from other indicators' periods (arbitrary, too noisy for this purpose); expanding-window warm-up average instead of NaN (statistically meaningless with only a few bars of history).

comments.summary: Non-blocking robustness note: `pct_deviation = (close - mid).abs() / mid` is an unguarded division by `mid`. A zero/near-zero EMA value (e.g. a data-provider gap filling `close` with 0.0) would silently produce inf/NaN that propagates through the rolling mean into `upper`/`lower` for the following `deviation_lookback` bars rather than raising. Low likelihood for real equity data, no consumer exists yet to exercise it (not wired into `portfolio-exit-rules` yet), and no sibling indicator (ema.py, macd.py, force_index.py) guards against degenerate zero-price input either. Flagged for whoever implements `portfolio-exit-rules`, not a blocker.

Non-blocking methodology note on the decision record: the chosen band width (exactly 1x trailing mean absolute % deviation, no multiplier) is a literal, faithful implementation of Analyse.md §4's stated formula ('EMA 13 ± avg % deviation'), and the checklist item correctly scoped this decision to window/rolling/symmetry/basis choices Analyse.md left open, not to second-guessing the formula shape itself. Worth naming anyway: a 1x-mean-absolute-deviation band is narrower than the '~90-95% of recent closes contained' envelope-sizing convention Elder actually describes in the source book, so price may touch/exceed the upper band more often than a rare 'overextension' signal implies. Not a gap in this task's decision -- flagged as a forward-looking note for `portfolio-exit-rules`, which actually consumes the upper-band-touch exit rule, in case it fires too eagerly in practice.
